latency_slo_targets: Non-streaming (completion end-to-end, client-observed): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms, p99 < 500ms
Streaming (initial token latency): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 380ms; tail for subsequent tokens target p95 < 100ms when using streaming chunks
Throughput-targeted tail SLO: maintain p95 latency while sustaining 150 concurrent RPS bursts for 2 minutes
Cold-cache penalty: allow up to +50ms p95 on first-token after model cold-start; plan for warm pools to reduce frequency
measurement_alignment: Require unified timing model: client-side end-to-end (HTTP request->first byte seen) will be source of truth for product SLAs
Server-side processing time will be exported (x-redwood-server-ms) for debugging and reconciliation
Agreement: Redwood will provide sample traces instrumented with request IDs; Silvercrest will sample at 5% for client SDK traces
Definition of streaming latency: initial-byte vs time-to-first-useful-token — agree to measure both and choose FTL (first useful token) for product alerts
Clock skew and TTL: use request IDs and server timestamps; both parties to normalize to UTC and align on NTP-synced windows for p95/p99 calculation
Aggregation window: rolling 1h p95 for alerting, daily p95/p99 for contractual SLA reporting
Sampling and instrumentation: Redwood SDK will add 'x-rcv-ts' header; Silvercrest to send client timing headers for reconciliation
reserved_gpu_planning: Baseline sizing ask: reserve 16x A100-equivalent GPUs for Dedicated pool (initial), expected sustained average 80 inference RPS with 40 concurrent long-lived sessions
Burst capacity: add 25% burst headroom to handle market-open spikes (target headroom to 100 RPS sustained for 3 minutes)
Model profile: primary model is a quantized 70B variant (float16->8-bit) with fallback to 13B for extreme tail/budget routing
KV cache behavior: warm-pooling recommended for session-affinity to keep KV cache warm; estimate warm pool memory footprint 0.6x peak session memory
Autoscaling policy: predictable scheduled autoscale for 15:30-16:30 EST market open, plus reactive scale with 90s cool-down
Capacity validation: Redwood to run 2 workload sims (morning spike + steady) and provide latency-by-percentile matrices before procurement
sla_negotiation_points: Latency SLA bands: define p95 SLA for non-streaming at 250ms with credits if monthly p95 > 300ms
Availability SLA: 99.9% for dedicated pool, with financial credits at 99.5% and below
Maintenance windows: Redwood to provide 48h notice; critical patches allowed with 4h advance notice and agreed rollback plan
Fallback routing: automatic fallback to smaller model or hosted pool if dedicated pool reaches saturation — require explicit routing policy in contract
Incident runbooks & postmortem timing: 48h initial incident summary, full RCA within 14 days
Data handling: explicit clause for audit log retention (7 years) and KMS key custody during legal holds
